Learn Ekagra in a few steps
Try a short guide with sample data. Your real sessions stay unchanged.
Finish your current timer and close any save or setup flow before starting practice.
What would you like to learn?
How to start a focus session
Focus counts down from a duration. Stopwatch counts up when you prefer an open-ended session. Next sets up a practice focus session.
In Settings, choose a preset, move the slider, or enter a custom duration. We will practice with 25 minutes.
Choose your break duration here. This practice uses 5 minutes. Your real settings will stay unchanged.
Start begins your focus session. Next demonstrates a running timer without starting a real session.
Pause stops the timer until you resume. End lets you save the session. Break starts your rest timer.
Resume continues the session you paused. Pausing does not mean finishing or saving your work.
During focus, Break starts your configured rest timer. End break returns you to focus. Next demonstrates returning to your session.
You are back in your practice focus session. Use Break whenever you need a planned rest. Next shows how to finish.
End opens a confirmation before you organize your session. We have advanced the practice timer so no waiting is needed.
Continue ends the timer and opens the session save flow. Cancel lets you keep focusing. Next demonstrates Continue.
Add an optional session name and subject tag. You can save on its own or link a goal before saving. This example is sample data only.
Review the save destination and completion choice before confirming. This practice confirmation changes no goals, topics, or account data.
History shows your saved sessions and recorded focus time. This practice entry is read-only and will disappear when you leave.
Stopwatch counts upward. Start, Pause, Resume, and End work similarly, and your elapsed time can be saved when you finish.
Open Pomodoro from Settings to alternate focus and rest automatically. Next opens a practice setup.
Traditional uses the rhythm described in this setup. Switch to Custom when you want to choose durations and the number of loops.
Custom lets you set focus minutes, break minutes, and loops. This example uses 25 / 5 and four loops. Next previews the running cycle.
The timer follows the configured Pomodoro cycle. You can pause, resume, or end it using the normal timer controls.
Enable Kavach and choose distracting apps before focusing. Usage access and display-over-other-apps permissions are required. This preview grants no permissions.
Turn on the apps you want to block, then tap Save apps. Search and the selection shortcuts help with longer lists. These are sample apps only.
Ready means Kavach is configured. Active means protection is running. Always On may keep protection active outside sessions; unavailable means protection needs attention.
This shortcut opens YouTube Focus setup. Use the existing permission guide there, then select study content. The practice shortcut stays inside this tutorial.
Music opens the audio library. Browse categories and select a track. Preview controls play audio in normal use; this practice stays silent.
Theme changes the timer backdrop. Pick a look that helps you focus. Practice previews never replace your saved theme.
Use Audio in Settings or the volume action in the overflow menu to mute and unmute session audio.
Choose Sound or Vibrate for timer alerts. Android alarm access may be needed for reliable alerts; use the existing permission flow outside practice.
Enable automatic breaks if you want rest to begin when focus finishes. Turn it off to start breaks yourself.
Open the overflow menu and choose Enable floating timer or Floating timer settings. Android overlay permission is needed.
After setup, the floating timer helps you keep track while using other apps. This is an in-app illustration, not a real overlay.
Select an open goal in the save flow. Keep it open if you have more work left. The same session time is associated with that goal.
Mark a goal done when appropriate
Choose the completion option only when the goal is finished. Saving time and completing a goal are separate choices. This sample goal is not real.
A session launched from a planner topic keeps that topic association. You can save the time while leaving the topic open.
Mark the topic complete only after finishing its study work. Review the confirmation before saving.
Use Ekagra and Stopwatch categories to review each kind of session. Choose the session name, tags, and goal association in the save flow.
Filter History by All, Today, or a chosen date, then use subject tags to narrow the list. Filters only change what you see.
Join Group opens Study Circles when you have not joined one yet. You can also open Study Circles from the menu.
Return to the timer after joining. Hold the group card to switch circles; Live shows how many people are focusing.
Use Focus for a timed session.
Tap Next to start the practice timer.
Use Pause to stop briefly, or End to finish.
Tap Next to resume and try a break.
End the break to return to focus.
Use Break when you need a rest.
Choose End when your work is finished.
Choose Continue to finish the session.
Add a name and tag, then save.
Review your saved focus time here.
Choose Stopwatch to count time up.
Set focus, break, and loop count.
Follow each focus and break cycle.
Select apps, then tap Save apps.
Open YouTube Focus to set up study.
Choose a track from the audio library.
Choose a backdrop for your timer.
Use Audio to mute or unmute.
Choose Sound or Vibrate for alerts.
Turn on automatic breaks if needed.
Keep track of time over other apps.
Link a goal and keep it open.
Mark the goal done only when finished.
Save study time against your topic.
Mark the topic done when finished.
Filter sessions by date or subject.
Tap Join Group beside the timer.
Hold the group card to choose your circle.
Open Settings to change focus and break time.
Settings lets you change both timer durations. You can also choose alerts, automatic breaks, and Pomodoro here.
Use Music and Theme to make it yours.
Music lets you choose a track or silence. Theme changes the timer backdrop. Both are optional.
Open Kavach from the menu; choose With Ekagra.
With Ekagra protects you during focus sessions. Choose apps to block next. Usage access and display-over-other-apps access are required; use the separate permission guides if needed.
Use Join with code, or Join on a public circle.
Ask a friend for a private circle’s code, or join a public circle from the list. This guide joins no real circle.
Choose Create circle, then Public or Private.
Public circles can be found by others. Private circles use an invite code. Creating a circle may require access on your plan. No circle is created in practice.
Choose a short guide. Practice uses sample data.
Sign in to try the feature guides.
